name: Essential Free Shipping Bar
summary: Shopify free-shipping progress bar for the top bar, product pages and cart, with cart goals, upsell products, geo-targeting and product exclusions; the free-shipping rate itself is set in Shopify.
best_for: Shopify stores that already offer free shipping above a threshold and want a no-code progress bar on the top bar or product pages, and that will pay $14.99 once they want it in the cart with upsell products next to it
skip_if: you want the progress bar in the cart without paying, because cart-page boosters start at $14.99 a month; you expect the app to create the free-shipping offer itself, since the rate has to be set in Shopify for each market; or your cart drawer app already has a reward or shipping bar built in
honest_knock:
The cart page, where a free-shipping progress bar does most of its work, is not on the free plan and not on Starter either. Cart-page boosters start on Essential at $14.99 a month; Free and Starter cover the top bar and product pages. One merchant uninstalled within an hour over exactly that in February 2026, calling it the obvious place for the bar; the vendor replied that the limits are on the listing, which is true. Upsell products inside the bar and the revenue analytics the listing advertises are on the same $14.99 tier.

The app shows the goal; it does not give the free shipping. The help centre says the app does not touch your store settings, so you set the free-shipping rate yourself in Shopify's shipping settings, as a conditional rate based on order price, and you do it again for every market. If the threshold in the bar and the threshold in Shopify drift apart, the bar promises something checkout does not deliver. Currencies work the same way: a currency missing from the dropdown needs its own Shopify Market first.

Views are counted on every load of every widget, and the free plan's 1,000 a month is small for a bar that sits on every product page. The help centre says Preview mode and the theme customiser are not counted; one merchant wrote in March 2026 that editing product pages in the customiser used up views, so check the counter after a design session. Past the limit there is no charge, but three days after the warning email the banners are unpublished until the 1st.

Two older complaints are worth knowing. A merchant in Japan wrote that the bar did not update when a shopper switched variants and prices; the vendor answered that real-time variant updates are supported and offered to help. And a UK merchant wrote in 2023 that uninstalling left code behind in the theme. Check the theme after removal.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/essential-order-value-booster and in our own test the same day; read 2026-09-29 there, on essential-apps.com/free-shipping-bar and in the vendor's help articles on views and on setup) Four plans priced on monthly booster views. Free covers up to 1,000 views a month with unlimited top-bar and product-page boosters. Starter is $9.99 a month for up to 10,000 views and adds geolocation targeting and excluding products from the goal. Essential is $14.99 a month for up to 50,000 views and adds cart-page boosters, upsell products inside the bar and analytics. Professional is $29.99 a month for unlimited views and every premium feature. Paid plans carry a 7-day free trial. The listing shows monthly prices only; the help centre says a yearly billing cycle can be chosen inside the app, and we found no published yearly price. A view is counted each time the widget loads, not per visitor; the help centre says Preview mode and the theme customiser are not counted. There is no overage charge: past the limit you get an email, and if you do not upgrade within 3 days the banners are unpublished until views reset on the 1st. All charges are in USD, billed through Shopify every 30 days. Developer Essential Apps, with an address in Vilnius, Lithuania; the listing gives a launch date of 3 June 2022 and showed 964 reviews on 29 September 2026 and 994 at 5.0 on 17 November 2026. The listing now counts “progress bar views” where it said booster views, and once installed the app is called “Essential Free Shipping” in the Shopify admin. In our own test that day the plan page showed the same four amounts and view limits, and Shopify's approval screen for Starter asked for a payment method.

schema_offer.description: Starter, per month for up to 10,000 booster views; free plan up to 1,000 views on top bar and product page only; Essential is $14.99 for 50,000 views and the cart page, Professional $29.99 for unlimited views; billed through Shopify every 30 days. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-17.

price_history.method: Stable = every amount on the vendor's pricing page identical across >= 3 of our reads over >= 30 days. A change is listed only after we confirmed the new price on the page, with a verbatim quote. Differences in raw readings are never published on their own.

free_plan_evidence: Free covers up to 1,000 views a month with unlimited top-bar and product-page boosters.

compare_with.name: Kite
compare_with.why: Kite is the closest app in our own dossiers with a progress bar, and the difference is what sits behind the bar. On our reading of 17 September 2026 Kite applied the reward itself - free gifts, buy X get Y and tiered discounts on native Shopify Functions - with progress bars from its $29 Starter plan and a free plan capped at 50 discount orders a month. Essential Free Shipping Bar only shows the goal: it starts free at 1,000 views and charges $9.99, $14.99 or $29.99 for more views, and the free shipping itself is a rate you set in Shopify. A store that wants one message - spend this much for free shipping - fits Essential at a fraction of the price; a store that wants the bar to offer gifts and discounts it cannot configure in Shopify's shipping settings fits Kite.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Essential Free Shipping (listed as Essential Free Shipping Bar) on a Shopify development store: the install through the install form, the free plan without a card or plan screen, a free shipping booster with a threshold of $75 that was published in the app after 4 clicks and 1 entry, then the bar Congratulations! You've got free shipping! at the top of an unsaved theme preview after the app embed was switched on by hand (about 2.5 minutes and 9 to 10 clicks from the install; the cart already held more than $75, so the text for the amount still to go was not seen; the embed was switched off again), the Pricing plans page with the free plan and three paid plans, the Shopify approval screen for Starter (a 7-day trial; it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The live store, a cart below the threshold and the paid features were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the app was installed from its own tab through the install form with the target set to the same tab, at about 21:27 (Mac clock; 21:26:42 was just before the form). In the Shopify admin the app is called Essential Free Shipping (the App Store handle is essential-order-value-booster, the review calls it Essential Free Shipping Bar). The screen Install app said that the app needs access to View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, discounts, Online Store); Install was clicked. There was no onboarding, no terms tick box and no payment step: the app opened at once on Your order value boosters with the plan Free. No account on the vendor site, password, card or phone number was asked. Core action, a free shipping bar with a threshold: at 21:28:26 the booster editor was reached through Create a new booster and Announcement (the top bar type). The default was Cart total 50 USD with the reward Free shipping, and the preview in the app said Free shipping for orders over $50.00!. The threshold was set to 75 and Publish was clicked: Booster saved, status Published, preview Free shipping for orders over $75.00!. That took 4 clicks and 1 entry in the app. A yellow note said Essential Free Shipping Bar app is not activated yet, with the buttons Activate and I have done it. In the theme editor (App embeds) the embed Free shipping bar / Essential Free Shipping was switched on and not saved. At 21:28:59 the bar stood at the top of the store preview with the text Congratulations! You've got free shipping!. The development store already had a cart with 3 items above 75 USD, so the bar showed the reached text and NOT the text for the amount still to go; that second text was not seen. From the install to the bar in the preview took about 2.5 minutes and 9 to 10 clicks. The embed was switched off again, the theme was not saved (Leave page was chosen at the unsaved changes question), and the published booster itself stayed in the app until the uninstall. No page of the live store was looked at, because the store has a password; the app does not change the free shipping rate in Shopify and whether that rate must be set up there was not tested. Plans in the app (Pricing plans): You're currently on Free (0 / 1000 monthly views). One visitor can have multiple views per session. Free Plan: Up to 1000 monthly views, Unlimited Top-bar boosters and Unlimited Product page boosters. Starter $9.99 a month: up to 10000 monthly views, Everything in Free, Geolocation targeting and Exclude products. Essential (Popular) $14.99 a month: up to 50000 monthly views, Everything in Starter, Unlimited cart page boosters, Add upsell products, Translations, Adding booster using product tags and Analytics. Professional $29.99 a month: Unlimited booster views, All premium features, unlimited product, top bar and cart page boosters, and Upsells & Analytics. Each paid plan has Start FREE 7-days trial. In the booster choice the Cart page type said Available with Essential plan, and in the editor Multiple goals are available from the Essential plan and Advanced product and country targeting available on Starter plan. No yearly view was noted. Checkout: Start FREE 7-days trial on Starter opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the plan starter, $9,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $9,99 Due 24 Nov, a row Add payment method and the line By proceeding, you are agreeing to the Terms of Service. The Approve button was greyed out. The screen did NOT say that a test charge would not be billed, and a payment method was needed. No card was entered and nothing was approved; Cancel was clicked. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was nothing to cancel in the app. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps and Uninstall: the dialog says that you can no longer use the app and that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and it asks for a Reason for uninstalling (Select all that apply); the reason Testing multiple apps was chosen. Differences from the review: the prices and the limits match the review (Free 1,000 views, Starter $9.99 for 10,000, Essential $14.99 for 50,000, Professional $29.99 unlimited); the app is called Essential Free Shipping in the admin. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: what the bar shows when the cart is below the threshold, the live store (it has a password), the cart page bar and the upsell in the bar (Essential), geolocation targeting and excluding products (Starter), whether the free shipping rate must be set up in Shopify, the view counting and what happens at the limit, the yearly prices, the paid plans and the payment. Clean up: the embed was switched off and the theme was not saved. The booster went with the uninstall. The app was uninstalled on 17 November through Settings, Apps and no longer showed in the list. No card was entered and nothing was approved. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The published booster did not show on the store until the app embed was switched on by hand in the theme editor; the app says so in a note after publishing. The app is called Essential Free Shipping in the admin, Essential Order Value Booster in the App Store address and Essential Free Shipping Bar in the review. The app does not change the free shipping rate in Shopify, according to our notes it was not tested whether that must be set up there.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Essential Free Shipping (listed as Essential Free Shipping Bar) on a Shopify development store: the install through the install form, the free plan without a card or plan screen, a free shipping booster with a threshold of $75 that was published in the app after 4 clicks and 1 entry, then the bar Congratulations! You've got free shipping! at the top of an unsaved theme preview after the app embed was switched on by hand (about 2.5 minutes and 9 to 10 clicks from the install; the cart already held more than $75, so the text for the amount still to go was not seen; the embed was switched off again), the Pricing plans page with the free plan and three paid plans, the Shopify approval screen for Starter (a 7-day trial; it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The live store, a cart below the threshold and the paid features were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the app was installed from its own tab through the install form with the target set to the same tab, at about 21:27 (Mac clock; 21:26:42 was just before the form). In the Shopify admin the app is called Essential Free Shipping (the App Store handle is essential-order-value-booster, the review calls it Essential Free Shipping Bar). The screen Install app said that the app needs access to View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, discounts, Online Store); Install was clicked. There was no onboarding, no terms tick box and no payment step: the app opened at once on Your order value boosters with the plan Free. No account on the vendor site, password, card or phone number was asked. Core action, a free shipping bar with a threshold: at 21:28:26 the booster editor was reached through Create a new booster and Announcement (the top bar type). The default was Cart total 50 USD with the reward Free shipping, and the preview in the app said Free shipping for orders over $50.00!. The threshold was set to 75 and Publish was clicked: Booster saved, status Published, preview Free shipping for orders over $75.00!. That took 4 clicks and 1 entry in the app. A yellow note said Essential Free Shipping Bar app is not activated yet, with the buttons Activate and I have done it. In the theme editor (App embeds) the embed Free shipping bar / Essential Free Shipping was switched on and not saved. At 21:28:59 the bar stood at the top of the store preview with the text Congratulations! You've got free shipping!. The development store already had a cart with 3 items above 75 USD, so the bar showed the reached text and NOT the text for the amount still to go; that second text was not seen. From the install to the bar in the preview took about 2.5 minutes and 9 to 10 clicks. The embed was switched off again, the theme was not saved (Leave page was chosen at the unsaved changes question), and the published booster itself stayed in the app until the uninstall. No page of the live store was looked at, because the store has a password; the app does not change the free shipping rate in Shopify and whether that rate must be set up there was not tested. Plans in the app (Pricing plans): You're currently on Free (0 / 1000 monthly views). One visitor can have multiple views per session. Free Plan: Up to 1000 monthly views, Unlimited Top-bar boosters and Unlimited Product page boosters. Starter $9.99 a month: up to 10000 monthly views, Everything in Free, Geolocation targeting and Exclude products. Essential (Popular) $14.99 a month: up to 50000 monthly views, Everything in Starter, Unlimited cart page boosters, Add upsell products, Translations, Adding booster using product tags and Analytics. Professional $29.99 a month: Unlimited booster views, All premium features, unlimited product, top bar and cart page boosters, and Upsells & Analytics. Each paid plan has Start FREE 7-days trial. In the booster choice the Cart page type said Available with Essential plan, and in the editor Multiple goals are available from the Essential plan and Advanced product and country targeting available on Starter plan. No yearly view was noted. Checkout: Start FREE 7-days trial on Starter opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the plan starter, $9,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $9,99 Due 24 Nov, a row Add payment method and the line By proceeding, you are agreeing to the Terms of Service. The Approve button was greyed out. The screen did NOT say that a test charge would not be billed, and a payment method was needed. No card was entered and nothing was approved; Cancel was clicked. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was nothing to cancel in the app. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps and Uninstall: the dialog says that you can no longer use the app and that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and it asks for a Reason for uninstalling (Select all that apply); the reason Testing multiple apps was chosen. Differences from the review: the prices and the limits match the review (Free 1,000 views, Starter $9.99 for 10,000, Essential $14.99 for 50,000, Professional $29.99 unlimited); the app is called Essential Free Shipping in the admin. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: what the bar shows when the cart is below the threshold, the live store (it has a password), the cart page bar and the upsell in the bar (Essential), geolocation targeting and excluding products (Starter), whether the free shipping rate must be set up in Shopify, the view counting and what happens at the limit, the yearly prices, the paid plans and the payment. Clean up: the embed was switched off and the theme was not saved. The booster went with the uninstall. The app was uninstalled on 17 November through Settings, Apps and no longer showed in the list. No card was entered and nothing was approved. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

What we saw: The Pricing plans page shows the Free Plan with Up to 1000 monthly views, Unlimited Top-bar boosters and Unlimited Product page boosters, and the line You're currently on Free (0 / 1000 monthly views). The app opened on this plan without a card, and a top bar booster was made and published on it. The limit was not used up and unlimited was not tried.

Text we checked: "Starter $9.99 /month: Up to 10000 monthly views". What we saw: The Starter column shows $9.99 a month with up to 10000 monthly views, Everything in Free, Geolocation targeting and Exclude products, and the editor said Advanced product and country targeting available on Starter plan. The Starter features were not used.

Text we checked: "Essential (Popular) $14.99 /month: Up to 50000 monthly views". What we saw: The Essential column shows $14.99 a month with up to 50000 monthly views, Unlimited cart page boosters, Add upsell products, Translations, Adding booster using product tags and Analytics, and the type Cart page said Available with Essential plan when choosing the booster. No Essential feature was used.

Text we checked: "Professional $29.99 /month: Unlimited booster views". What we saw: The Professional column shows $29.99 a month with Unlimited booster views and All premium features. Its approval screen was not opened and the plan was not started.

Text we checked: "Free shipping for orders over $75.00!". What we saw: With the threshold set to 75 and Publish clicked, the app said Booster saved with the status Published and showed the preview Free shipping for orders over $75.00!. The default threshold was 50 USD. This took 4 clicks and 1 entry in the app.
